description: A mathematically-inclined student who mastered C++ through competitive programming and is now pursuing a career in theoretical computer science research.

nodes.description: Review of C++ object-oriented principles including inheritance, polymorphism, and class design patterns using the Goodrich textbook.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has strong_prior_exposure, we skip basic syntax and focus immediately on high-level architectural design in C++.
nodes.title: Advanced Object-Oriented Design in C++
Enrichment: Move Semantics & RAII
nodes.description: In-depth exploration of Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII) and move semantics to optimize performance and memory safety.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Student's strong_prior_exposure allows us to replace basic pointer scaffolding with advanced memory management techniques.

nodes.title: Enrichment: Generic Programming with Templates
nodes.description: Advanced use of C++ templates for generic programming, including template specialization and recursion.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Leveraging the student's strong_prior_exposure to delve into template metaprogramming, a core part of the STL used throughout the course.

nodes.title: Linked List Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: Student's strong_prior_exposure suggests they can quickly master manual memory allocation for linked structures.
nodes.description: Implementation and performance analysis of singly and doubly linked lists within the C++ memory model.

nodes.title: Recursion and Asymptotic Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: With strong_prior_exposure to programming, the student is ready to formalize algorithm performance using asymptotic notation.
nodes.description: Analysis of recursive algorithms and introduction to Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notations.

nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard assessment for block 02 to ensure the student with strong_prior_exposure has mastered recursion.
nodes.description: Assessment covering recursion and linked list concepts.

nodes.title: Stacks and Queues ADTs
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because of their strong_prior_exposure, the student will focus on comparing the efficiency of different implementation strategies.
nodes.description: Abstract Data Types (ADTs) for Stacks and Queues, including array-based and list-based implementations.
Deep dive into the C++ STL Vector, dynamic arrays, and the iterator pattern for sequence traversal.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Student's strong_prior_exposure facilitates a faster transition from using vectors to understanding their internal resizing logic.
nodes.title: Vectors and Iterators
Sequences and Bubble Sort
nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure ensures the student can efficiently bridge sequence ADTs with basic sorting algorithms.
nodes.description: Introduction to simple sorting via Bubble Sort and its relationship to sequence-based data structures.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory midterm review assessment tailored to the student's progress despite their strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of material from blocks 01-03 in preparation for the midterm exam.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Assessment
General Trees and Traversal
nodes.personalizationRationale: Student's strong_prior_exposure allows for a quick grasp of hierarchical data structures.
nodes.description: General tree structures, definitions, and standard traversal algorithms (pre-order, post-order).
Properties, representations, and traversal of binary trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Binary trees are a core course requirement that students with strong_prior_exposure must master for later balanced tree topics.
nodes.title: Binary Trees

nodes.description: Heaps as an implementation of the Priority Queue ADT, including heap-sort logic.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Focuses on the efficiency of the heap-ify process, suitable for a student with strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Priority Queues and Heaps

nodes.description: Hash functions, collision resolution strategies, and the Map ADT implementation.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure students explore the mathematical properties of hash functions in addition to standard usage.
nodes.title: Maps and Hash Tables

nodes.personalizationRationale: Required quiz for block 06 to verify mastery of hash-based structures.
nodes.description: Assessment focused on hashing and map structures.
nodes.title: Quiz 3: Hashing

nodes.description: Implementation of Binary Search Trees (BST) and self-balancing AVL tree rotations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: A student with strong_prior_exposure can focus on the algorithmic proofs of AVL balance.
nodes.title: BST and AVL Trees
Red-Black and Multi-Way Trees
nodes.description: Advanced tree structures including Multi-way Search Trees and Red-Black Trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core required content for all students; strong_prior_exposure helps with understanding complex pointer manipulations.
Student with strong_prior_exposure will focus on the divide-and-conquer proof of Merge Sort.
nodes.description: Analysis and implementation of Merge Sort and Selection Sort algorithms.
nodes.title: Sorting Algorithms: Merge and Selection Sort
Quiz 4: Sorting
nodes.description: Final quiz covering sorting and capstone topics.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Final required quiz for block 08 content.

nodes.description: Comprehensive review of all course material (blocks 01-08) for the final exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory cumulative review for the final exam, ensuring students with strong_prior_exposure integrate all concepts.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review
